key_insight: Context-Aware Folding (CAF) improves portfolio optimization by injecting compressed global risk context into each local quantum-classical subproblem, reducing the loss from purely local decomposition.
engineering_relevance: CAF is a lightweight coordination layer that can sit between decomposition and solver execution, making large-scale portfolio optimization more practical across classical, quantum-inspired, and NISQ backends.
method: Compress global covariance/risk into a shared state.
Add a state-dependent linear bias to each local subproblem.
Use sequential acceptance to commit candidates with monotonic non-divergence.
evidence_signal: On a 2016 Russell 3000 subset (N=484), CAF with SA improved the scalarized mean-variance objective by 6.59% over a static baseline with 20/20 wins, with additional gains on a 2018 panel (N=1397) and compatibility tests for QAOA/SQA plus one frozen hardware run on Wukong 180.
watch_item: Performance depends on how well the compressed global state preserves cross-cluster covariance, and the hardware result is limited to a single warm-started small subproblem.
paper_title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Coordination Architecture for Portfolio Optimization via Global Context Injection
